summary: A Netflix list of seven Indian thrillers. It may suit her taste for suspense and strong narrative, though it reads as a promotional listicle with no detail on the titles.

title: How carbon credits helped unlock the Great Koala National Park in NSW
summary: After more than a decade of campaigning and three state elections, New South Wales has created the Great Koala National Park, the state's second-largest national park. The piece explains how carbon credits helped make it possible, a concrete conservation win.

title: Astronomers discovered first green star ever. And it’s powered by a dead planet’s chemistry.
summary: Astronomers have identified what is described as the first green star, a finding the article links to chemistry left behind by a dead planet. It is a lovely piece of science with a striking image of the night sky, suited to a reader who loves vivid prose.

title: 10 Art Books to Curl Up With This November
summary: A Hyperallergic roundup of art books for autumn reading, including a Celia Paul essay collection written from Venice, a study of Salman Toor's painted worlds, and the secret herbarium of Rosa Luxemburg. The text is brief, but the mix of essays and history suits a reader who likes art linked to writing.

title: Video of two brothers Irish step dancing to Beyoncé’s country hit ‘Texas Hold ‘Em’ is pure delight
summary: A short video of the Gardiner Brothers performing Irish step dance to Beyoncé's country track "Texas Hold 'Em". It is a joyful blend of dance and music, the kind of thing that lifts a morning.

title: Grandmaster Flash, one of the founding fathers of hip-hop, talks about his life in music.
summary: BBC Radio 4's Front Row features Grandmaster Flash discussing his memoir Birth of a Culture, alongside a segment on the Ramayana's cultural and literary significance as a new film appears. The literary strand may interest you, though the programme also covers Patrick Stewart.

title: Whale Festival Kicks Off on Amelia Island in Florida Celebrating the Return of the Right Whale
summary: Early November 2026, Amelia Island, Florida: the annual Right Whale Festival, held since 2009, celebrates the seasonal return of one of the world's most endangered whale species. The good news is conservation, though it is a long way from Belledonne.

title: Travail forcé, enfants volés : l’Irlande au tribunal | Documentaire | ARTE
summary: An ARTE documentary on the Justice for Magdalenes campaign, which has pressed for the rights of women held in Irish mother-and-baby homes and laundries from 1922 to 1996. It offers a hard, well-documented piece of recent history that resonates with novels such as Philomena.

title: Ana Mendieta's Lasting Imprint on Art
summary: A major survey at Tate Modern revisits Ana Mendieta's work, which centres on the earth, the female body and her distinctive practice. It is a strong art-history piece, and the London show suits a British-section teacher.

title: Bourgoin-Jallieu. L'exposition sur Tim Burton fait un carton : « Je suis fan depuis le début »
summary: A Tim Burton exhibition in Bourgoin-Jallieu, Isère, is proving a hit with visitors. The available text is a headline only, so the details of the show are not known from this piece.

title: À la fondation Cartier, Ibrahim Mahama et les artistes de la scène artistique ghanéenne inventent un autre futur
summary: Until February, at the Fondation Cartier in Paris, Ibrahim Mahama and artists from the Ghanaian scene present a large exhibition imagining another future. The text is cut short, but it is a substantial show by a leading contemporary artist.

title: New on Netflix: The 8 best movies and shows in November, from 'Black Doves' to 'The Hunting Wives'
summary: A Yahoo roundup of the best new Netflix films and series for November, naming Black Doves and The Hunting Wives. Yamuna enjoys thrillers, so the list is worth opening, though the text itself is only a headline.

title: Thousands of young doctors deployed to France's 'medical deserts'
summary: From 3 November, almost 3,000 young doctors take up posts in areas short of doctors, many in rural France, so that patients can more easily get appointments. A hopeful piece about access to care in the countryside.

title: Les enfants délaissés de la Chine | Documentaire | ARTE
summary: Available on ARTE until 29 May 2027, this documentary follows Qui Che, a 14-year-old whose mother works in Hangzhou while he lives with his grandparents in a remote Yunnan village. It shows, through one child's story, the wider situation of around 67 million left-behind children in China.

title: Beaches, Beatles and a broken marriage: how Wilhelmina Barns-Graham became a radical art icon
summary: A retrospective of the British modernist Wilhelmina Barns-Graham has opened at Tate St Ives, with her large Glacier (Blue Cave) at its centre. The piece explores an artist long sidelined from St Ives' art history, inspired by glaciers, Vietnam and her own divorce.

title: Strangers Ran Towards the Fire to Save Teen–Her Mom Now Funds Scholarships for Heroes Like Them
summary: Four men ran into a fire on a Texas highway to pull an 18-year-old from her burning car, and one of them, Mike Argote, was burned. The teen's mother now funds scholarships for people like them. It is a clear story of ordinary kindness.

title: Crossings: Laura Pannack’s award-winning images of South African youth – in pictures
summary: Laura Pannack has won the inaugural Tom Stoddart award for her project Crossings, which follows young people in South Africa on their journeys to and from school. The photographs document the physical and psychological challenges of those journeys.

title: À Grenoble, Mistral se raconte avec ses habitants
summary: In Grenoble, a project has residents telling the story of the Mistral district in their own words. The text is brief, but it suggests a piece of local life and memory.

title: Lit Hub Daily: November 2, 2026
summary: Lit Hub's daily digest includes a critical essay on Agnes Owens's Scottish working-class novel How A Working Mother, which finds 'the surrealness of everyday life' in its pages. It also offers children's book recommendations for November.

title: Apiculture : des abeilles résistantes aux parasites | ARTE Regards
summary: Available on ARTE until 25 January 2027, this 30-minute German report follows beekeeper Christian Schneider as he investigates why honeybees in north-west Wales resist the varroa mite, which threatens bees across Europe. It is a clear and hopeful piece of nature reporting.

title: “Attempts to restore Brookner’s reputation” – Anita Brookner: Art and Life by Hermione Lee
summary: A Bookmunch review of Hermione Lee's biography Anita Brookner: Art and Life, which looks at the novelist's life alongside her art and at efforts to restore her reputation. The text is only a title, but it suits your interest in the links between painting and fiction.

title: 7 of the best new and returning shows to watch in November, including a brilliant Netflix hit
summary: A roundup of the best new and returning shows for November, one of them a Netflix hit. The text is only the headline, so the individual titles are not clear from this item. It is worth a look for ideas on what to start next.

title: Roadtrip : Soif de liberté | Twist | ARTE
summary: An ARTE episode of the Twist series, available until 25 October 2027. It follows photographer Kourtney Roy, street musician Borja Catanesi and Dario J. Lagana on road trips, including Spain and Iceland, and asks what happens when the romantic dream meets reality. It suits her interest in photography, music and travel on ARTE.

title: Kazuo Ishiguro, Unlocked: The Butler as Metaphor
summary: A Paris Review essay on Kazuo Ishiguro's method, centred on how he inhabits his characters, with the butler as a metaphor. The excerpt is brief, but the piece suits a reader who values narrators and the craft of character.
